strengths: Significance and basic soundness: Clustering weakly connected directed graphs is a useful problem. Given a stochastic P and strictly positive vertex measure, Equation (3) provides a valid reversible operator with stationary measure proportional to ν + νᵀP and connectivity inherited from the underlying undirected graph.

Empirical merits: Table 3 reports meaningful improvements on the DiSBM Chain benchmark (0.93 AMI versus 0.85 for the strongest baseline) and PolBlogs (0.39 versus 0.21). The experiments varying flow strength, cluster size, and degree heterogeneity provide useful evidence about settings where the method may help.

Originality: Combining vertex-measure operators with multiple-vector power iteration and sampled entropy selection constitutes a coherent practical extension of PIC. Applying the same projection and time-selection procedures to the PIC baselines helps isolate differences between operators.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 communicate the pipeline clearly. Dataset statistics, synthetic model parameters, repeated-run results, and sensitivity analyses are useful. The discussion acknowledges parameter sensitivity and irregular entropy curves. No material research-ethics concern is apparent from the described experiments.
weaknesses: Soundness: Proposition 3.5 is false, including under reversibility, irreducibility, and aperiodicity. Take P = [[0.99, 0.01], [0.5, 0.5]] and ν = (50/51, 1/51). Equation (3) gives P(ν) = P, yet the stated entropy decreases from H(1) = 0.74915 to H(2) = 0.64523. Appendix E applies Jensen’s inequality incorrectly; row stochasticity does not imply the claimed entropy increase. This invalidates the theoretical justification for a central component, although entropy selection could still be evaluated as a heuristic.

Soundness of the diffusion interpretation: Equations (5) and (19) use P(ν) = ΦΛΦᵀ for a generally nonsymmetric reversible matrix, omitting the stationary-distribution weighting required by its spectral decomposition. Appendix E also uses reciprocal stationary weights where the stated orthogonality requires stationary weights. More substantively, Algorithm 1 clusters unweighted rows of P(ν)^t or their random projections, whereas Equation (4) defines a distance weighted by 1/π(ν). The practical embedding therefore does not implement the stated diffusion geometry.

Implementation and supported graph class: Equation (9) computes a column of P(ν)^t, rather than the claimed row, so the sampled entropy algorithm is incorrect as written. Furthermore, P = D_out⁻¹W is undefined at sinks, which the manuscript explicitly identifies in its real benchmarks. No stochastic treatment of dangling vertices is specified; simply retaining zero rows would make Equation (3) substochastic. These omissions directly affect the advertised applicability to weakly connected digraphs.

Scalability: The claimed O(N^(3/2)) complexity on dense graphs is incorrect for the described implementation. With m nonzeros and projection dimension d, repeated multiplication costs O(tmd); d = √N gives O(tN^(5/2)) on dense graphs. The smaller bound requires m = O(N). Comparisons also treat spectral clustering as requiring a full cubic eigendecomposition, without establishing an advantage over partial iterative eigensolvers. Figure 3, extending only to roughly 7,000 vertices, does not resolve these concerns.

Evaluation and reproducibility: Appendix B.2 defines the reverse-edge branch of the Simple-Herm matrix using W_ij when its condition explicitly sets W_ij = 0. Consequently, that matrix is not Hermitian as claimed. It is unclear whether this is a transcription error or an implementation error affecting the comparisons. Code is deferred until publication, and preprocessing, k-means settings, runtime hardware, and the entropy search horizon and fallback rules are insufficiently specified to resolve these ambiguities.

Scope and presentation of claims: Equation (3) constructs a walk on the symmetric affinity DνP + PᵀDν. It retains information through weights derived from directions while discarding nonreversible currents; claims of preserving directional dynamics need qualification and a sharper distinction from the cited vertex-measure framework. Empirical claims also exceed the evidence: Table 2 ties S-PIC overall, Email Eu slightly favors S-PIC, and Figure 7(e) places the entropy-selected time after the highest-AMI interval despite claims of consistently competitive selection. The central guarantees and comparisons require correction and revalidation before acceptance.
